L424: ## File systemcite2†# L425: 
L426: Source Code: cite414†lib/fs.js†github.com L427: 
L428: cite415†Stability: 2 - Stable
L429: 
L430: The `node:fs` module enables interacting with the file system in a way modeled on standard POSIX functions.
L431: 
L432: To use the promise-based APIs:
L433: 
L434:     [Input]`import * as fs from 'node:fs/promises';
L435:     ``const fs = require('node:fs/promises');
L436:     `
L437: 
L438:     javascript[Button: copy]
L439: To use the callback and sync APIs:
L440: 
L441:     [Input]`import * as fs from 'node:fs';
L442:     ``const fs = require('node:fs');
L443:     `
L444: 
L445:     javascript[Button: copy]
L446: 
L447: All file system operations have synchronous, callback, and promise-based forms, and are accessible using both CommonJS syntax and ES6 Modules (ESM).
L448: ### Promise examplecite3†# L449: Promise-based operations return a promise that is fulfilled when the asynchronous operation is complete.
L450: 
L451:     [Input]`import { unlink } from 'node:fs/promises';
L452: 
L453:     try {
L454:       await unlink('/tmp/hello');
L455:       console.log('successfully deleted /tmp/hello');
L456:     } catch (error) {
L457:       console.error('there was an error:', error.message);
L458:     }
L459:     ``const { unlink } = require('node:fs/promises');
L460: 
L461:     (async function(path) {
L462:       try {
L463:         await unlink(path);
L464:         console.log(`successfully deleted ${path}`);
L465:       } catch (error) {
L466:         console.error('there was an error:', error.message);
L467:       }
L468:     })('/tmp/hello');
L469:     `
L470: 
L471:     javascript[Button: copy]
L472: ### Callback examplecite4†# L473: The callback form takes a completion callback function as its last argument and invokes the operation asynchronously. The arguments passed to the completion callback depend on the method, but the first argument is always reserved for an exception. If the operation is completed successfully, then the first argument is `null` or `undefined`.
L474: 
L475:     [Input]`import { unlink } from 'node:fs';
L476: 
L477:     unlink('/tmp/hello', (err) => {
L478:       if (err) throw err;
L479:       console.log('successfully deleted /tmp/hello');
L480:     });
L481:     ``const { unlink } = require('node:fs');
L482: 
L483:     unlink('/tmp/hello', (err) => {
L484:       if (err) throw err;
L485:       console.log('successfully deleted /tmp/hello');
L486:     });
L487:     `
L488: 
L489:     javascript[Button: copy]
L490: The callback-based versions of the `node:fs` module APIs are preferable over the use of the promise APIs when maximal performance (both in terms of execution time and memory allocation) is required.
L491: ### Synchronous examplecite5†# L492: The synchronous APIs block the Node.js event loop and further JavaScript execution until the operation is complete. Exceptions are thrown immediately and can be handled using `try…catch`, or can be allowed to bubble up.
L493: 
L494:     [Input]`import { unlinkSync } from 'node:fs';
L495: 
L496:     try {
L497:       unlinkSync('/tmp/hello');
L498:       console.log('successfully deleted /tmp/hello');
L499:     } catch (err) {
L500:       // handle the error
L501:     }
L502:     ``const { unlinkSync } = require('node:fs');
L503: 
L504:     try {
L505:       unlinkSync('/tmp/hello');
L506:       console.log('successfully deleted /tmp/hello');
L507:     } catch (err) {
L508:       // handle the error
L509:     }
L510:     `
L511:

L522: The `fs/promises` API provides asynchronous file system methods that return promises.
L523: The promise APIs use the underlying Node.js threadpool to perform file system operations off the event loop thread. These operations are not synchronized or threadsafe. Care must be taken when performing multiple concurrent modifications on the same file or data corruption may occur.
